sourcedFrom: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. (2025 — ©2025 on the title page.)
cleanIntro: The R338 is KGM's titanium magnum can — 9.1 inches, 19 ounces, rated for .338 Lapua and .338 Norma — and it rides a 3/4x24 taper muzzle brake rather than threading straight onto the barrel. KGM publishes no way into the tube: the owner's maintenance is the mounting surfaces after every session, and a 24-hour soak every 2,000–3,000 rounds or once a year. Two things on this can are the owner's to look after besides cleaning: the taper seat between can and brake, which is where retention and alignment live, and the brake itself, which KGM calls sacrificial and expects to be replaced as it erodes. KGM's own fouling gauge is a kitchen scale — weigh it new, weigh it again later.

steps.title: Rifle unloaded before the can is touched
steps.action: KGM's first safety line covers mounting, removing, cleaning, storage and shipping in one sentence — the rifle is unloaded for all five. Magazine out, bolt open, chamber checked by eye and by finger before a hand goes near the muzzle end.
steps.quote: Ensure the host firearm is UNLOADED before mounting or removing the suppressor, cleaning, storage, or shipping
steps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Safety Precautions, printed p.2

steps.title: ⛔ Cool before it comes off
steps.action: A titanium can on a .338 magnum gets very hot and holds it. KGM puts the wait in the warning box above the removal procedure — leave it until it can be held bare-handed.
steps.quote: If suppressor is hot, wait for it to cool before attempting to remove.
steps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Removing Taper Mount Suppressor, printed p.7

steps.title: Grasp and turn counter-clockwise
steps.action: First try is by hand: grip the tube and turn it counter-clockwise. A taper seat that was snapped home properly will break loose with a firm twist and then spin freely.
steps.quote: Grasp suppressor and rotate counter-clockwise to loosen and remove.
steps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Removing Taper Mount Suppressor, printed p.7

steps.title: Stuck? Two wrenches, two sets of flats
steps.action: If it will not break by hand, KGM's answer is two wrenches at once — the suppressor wrench on the can's wrench flats at the rear of the tube, and a second wrench on the brake's own flats. The second wrench is what keeps the force off the brake's threads into the barrel; turning the can alone can back the brake off the muzzle instead.
steps.quote: If suppressor is firmly attached, use suppressor wrench on suppressor flats, and muzzle device wrench on muzzle device flats
steps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Removing Taper Mount Suppressor, printed p.7

steps.title: Unscrew while the brake is held still
steps.action: With the brake held from turning, unscrew the can counter-clockwise until its threads run out. The brake stays on the rifle — it is thread-locked in place and does not come off for routine cleaning.
steps.quote: Un-screw the suppressor suppressor in a counter-clockwise direction while holding muzzle device in place.
steps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Removing Taper Mount Suppressor, printed p.7

steps.title: Slide it straight off the brake
steps.action: Once the threads are clear, the can slides forward off the taper. Pull it straight, along the bore line — the taper surface is the alignment surface, and dragging the can off at an angle scuffs it.
steps.quote: Once the suppressor is free of the muzzle device threads, slide the suppressor off of the muzzle device.
steps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Removing Taper Mount Suppressor, printed p.7

steps.title: Mounting surfaces, every session
steps.action: This is KGM's whole routine job and it is about the joint, not the inside of the can: the can's rear threads and taper seat, and the brake's threads and taper surface. Carbon on either one stops the can seating fully, and a can that does not seat is a can that is not aligned.
steps.aside: Routine maintenance for KGM suppressors is minimal.
steps.quote: During standard host weapon maintenance, clean and inspect the mounting surfaces of both the suppressor and the muzzle device.
steps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Suppressor Maintenance — Regular Maintenance, printed p.10

steps.title: Brush what you can reach, then dry it
steps.action: A brush on the accessible surfaces for carbon and copper — the end cap, the bore openings, the rear of the can and the brake. Ordinary gun-cleaning chemicals are fine on this titanium can. Wipe it down or rinse it with water, and dry it before it goes back on.
steps.quote: Use a brush to eliminate carbon and copper fouling from accessible surfaces. Common gun cleaning chemicals are suitable. Wipe clean or rinse with water and dry.
steps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Suppressor Maintenance — Regular Maintenance, printed p.10

steps.title: Inspect the brake — it is meant to wear out
steps.action: Look at the brake's ports and crown for erosion every time the rifle is cleaned. KGM treats the brake as the part that takes the blast so the can does not, and expects it to be replaced. A worn brake is a reason to order a new one, not a reason to keep shooting it.
steps.aside: The muzzle device is a sacrificial component for heavy-use suppressors, and may require replacement due to erosion, particularly with short barreled rifles.
steps.quote: Periodically inspect the muzzle device during rifle maintenance and replace if necessary.
steps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Suppressor Maintenance — Muzzle Device, printed p.10

deepSteps.title: When the heavy clean is due
deepSteps.action: KGM's interval is 2,000 to 3,000 rounds, once a year, or sooner if it has fouled up or gone louder. Their gauge for fouling is weight: a can that has put on several ounces since it was new is due now, whatever the round count says.
deepSteps.aside: If several ounces have been accumulated, a heavy cleaning cycle should occur.
deepSteps.quote: Perform a more thorough cleaning cycle for the suppressor after several thousand rounds (2,000-3,000), on an annual basis, or as necessary due to fouling or loss of effectiveness.
deepSteps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Suppressor Maintenance — Heavy Cleaning, printed p.10

deepSteps.title: Into a container, or plugged and muzzle-down
deepSteps.action: Two ways to hold the fluid: the whole can in a chemically resistant container, or plug the end-cap end and stand the can on it so it holds the fluid itself.
deepSteps.quote: Place the suppressor in a chemically resistant container or plug the muzzle and position it muzzle-down inside the container.
deepSteps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Suppressor Maintenance — Heavy Cleaning, printed p.10

deepSteps.title: Fill and soak for 24 hours
deepSteps.action: Fill it with CLR, a 30% vinegar solution, or a comparable suppressor cleaner, and leave it a full day. KGM warns that some chemicals discolour the finish. An ultrasonic cleaner is also an option in their book, with the same discolouration risk and the chance of scratching.
deepSteps.quote: 30% Vinegar solution, OR similar suppressor cleaner, and soak for 24 hours.
deepSteps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Suppressor Maintenance — Heavy Cleaning, printed p.10
deepSteps.warn: NOTE 1: Certain cleaning solutions or chemicals may cause color discoloration.

deepSteps.title: Drain, rinse, brush, rinse again
deepSteps.action: Out of the container and drained. Rinse it through with water, brush whatever carbon the soak loosened at the openings, and rinse again.
deepSteps.aside: Brush any accessible carbon buildup and rinse with water again.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the suppressor from the container and drain of fluid.
deepSteps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Suppressor Maintenance — Heavy Cleaning, printed p.10

deepSteps.title: Air-dry the inside
deepSteps.action: Compressed air through the bore and the APEC ports until nothing more comes out. Water left in the baffles is what the next step has to blow out.
deepSteps.quote: Use compressed air to dry suppressor internals.
deepSteps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Suppressor Maintenance — Heavy Cleaning, printed p.10

deepSteps.title: Fire 5–10 rounds to clear it
deepSteps.action: KGM's last step is live fire: mount it properly on the rifle and shoot 5 to 10 rounds to push out loosened carbon and leftover fluid. Expect that first string to be dirty.
deepSteps.quote: Fire 5-10 rounds of live ammunition to expel any loosened carbon and remaining fluids.
deepSteps.cite: User Manual For KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM Taper Muzzle Brake Suppressors User Manual — Suppressor Maintenance — Heavy Cleaning, printed p.10

cleaning.name: TAPER SEAT AND THREADS (CAN AND BRAKE)
tasks: Can's rear threads and taper seat cleaned and inspected
Brake's threads and taper surface cleaned and inspected
No carbon left on either surface — it stops the can seating fully

cleaning.name: ACCESSIBLE SURFACES
tasks: Brush carbon and copper from the end cap and bore openings
Common gun-cleaning chemicals are suitable on this titanium can
Wipe clean or rinse with water, then dry

cleaning.name: TAPER MUZZLE BRAKE (SACRIFICIAL)
tasks: Ports and crown checked for erosion
Replace it when worn — KGM expects it to wear out
⛔ Never a crush washer under a suppressor mount

cleaning.name: ⛔ THE INTERVALS ARE THE MAINTENANCE
tasks: Heavy clean at 2,000–3,000 rounds, annually, or on loss of effectiveness
Weigh it new and weigh it again periodically — KGM's own fouling measure

reassembly: Action open and clear before the can goes back on.
Line the rear of the can up with the brake and slide it on until it meets the brake's threads.
Screw it on clockwise until it completely stops, then grip it firmly and tighten — back it off slightly and snap it home for the best hand-tight seat.
Suppressor wrench on the can's flats for additional torque, if wanted.
First fitting on a new rifle or a new brake: verify alignment with a properly fitting bore rod, and REMOVE THE ROD BEFORE FIRING.
fncheck: Back on the rifle with the action open and clear: line the rear of the can up with the brake and slide it on until it meets the threads, screw it on clockwise until it stops, then grip it firmly and tighten — KGM's tip is to back it off slightly and snap it home by hand. The suppressor wrench on the can's flats adds more torque if you want it. It must be fully seated on the brake. Before the first shot on a new rifle, or after the brake has been replaced, check alignment with a bore alignment rod that fits properly; if it is misaligned, call KGM rather than shooting it. ⛔ Take the rod out before you fire.
